t:
Section 5 of the Act of May 26, 1936 (49 Stat. 1372, 1373; 48 U. S. C., 1946 edition, sec. 1401d), is hereby amended to read as follows:

“The Virgin Islands Corporation shall pay annually into the municipal treasuries of the Virgin Islands in lieu of taxes an amount equal to the amount of taxes which would be payable on the real property in the Virgin Islands owned by the Virgin Islands Corporation, if such real property were in private ownership and taxable, but the valuation placed upon such property for taxation purposes by the local taxing authorities shall be reduced to a reasonable amount by the designee of the President of the United States as provided in section 1 of the Virgin Islands Corporation Act if, after investigation, he finds that such valuation is excessive and unreasonable, and any such reduction in valuation, together with the findings on which it is based, shall not be reviewable by any court. The Virgin Islands Corporation shall also pay into the municipal treasuries of the Virgin Islands amounts equal to the amounts of any taxes of general application which a private corporation similarly situated would be required to pay into the said treasuries. Similar payments shall be made with respect to any property owned by the United States in the Virgin Islands which is used for ordinary business or commercial purposes, and the income derived from any property so used shall be available for making such payments: Provided, however, That the payments authorized by this section shall not include payments in lieu of income taxes, capital stock taxes, or franchise taxes.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the local taxing authorities' valuation of the property brings a non-federal government into a federal decision. But the section only sets payments in lieu of taxes and lets the President's designee unilaterally reduce the local valuation after his own investigation, with no requirement to consult, hear from, or coordinate with local authorities or the public. It also expressly bars court review, so it grants no right to sue over the decision.
fable.s: any such reduction in valuation, together with the findings on which it is based, shall not be reviewable by any court

qwen_block.w: This section describes a process where a federal official (the designee of the President) investigates and adjusts property valuations for a corporation. It explicitly states that these decisions are 'not reviewable by any court,' which removes the right to sue or object. There is no requirement for consultation with the public, states, or other outside entities before the decision is made; the process is unilateral by the federal official. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: the valuation placed upon such property for taxation purposes by the local taxing authorities shall be reduced to a reasonable amount by the designee of the President of the United States as provided in section 1 of the Virgin Islands Corporation Act if, after investigation, he finds that such valuation is excessive and unreasonable, and any such reduction in valuation, together with the findings on which it is based, shall not be reviewable by any court.

opus.w: This section sets up payments in lieu of taxes and lets the President's designee reduce a valuation on his own after investigating it. It does not require any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body involving people outside the federal government. Local taxing authorities appear only as the source of the original valuation, not as participants in the federal decision. The court clause removes any right to sue over the reduction, so it is the opposite of granting an outside party a right to challenge the decision.
opus.s: shall be reduced to a reasonable amount by the designee of the President of the United States as provided in section 1 of the Virgin Islands Corporation Act if, after investigation, he finds that such valuation is excessive and unreasonable, and any such reduction in valuation, together with the findings on which it is based, shall not be reviewable by any court.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions "local taxing authorities," an "investigation," and court review, so it can look like outsiders take part in a federal decision. That reading fails on each point:
   - The local authorities only set the original tax valuation. The President's designee then decides on his own whether to reduce it, without being required to consult anyone outside the federal government.
   - The "investigation" is the federal official's own fact-finding.
   - The court language takes away any right to challenge the decision in court rather than granting one.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes an administrative process where a federal official (the designee of the President) determines property valuation based on their own investigation. There is no requirement for consultation with outside parties, public hearings, or advisory committees. Furthermore, the text explicitly states that the decision is not reviewable by any court, denying outside parties the right to sue or formally object. Therefore, no participation by non-federal entities is required or recommended.
qwen_chat.s: the valuation placed upon such property for taxation purposes by the local taxing authorities shall be reduced to a reasonable amount by the designee of the President of the United States as provided in section 1 of the Virgin Islands Corporation Act if, after investigation, he finds that such valuation is excessive and unreasonable, and any such reduction in valuation, together with the findings on which it is based, shall not be reviewable by any court.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "designee of the President" conducting an "investigation" implies a process where outside parties (the Virgin Islands Corporation or local authorities) participate. However, the text describes an administrative determination by a federal official based on their own investigation, with no requirement for public comment, hearings, or consultation with outside entities before the decision is made. The clause "shall not be reviewable by any court" explicitly removes the right to sue, which is a form of participation.
